clue.text: Carson's act, funny and above criticism

indicators.note: something funny is odd or peculiar, so these letters are set out in a strange new order

blocks.note: the letters of the phrase, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A comedian's routine is so amusing that no critic dares to fault it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sacrosanct is treated as too sacred or important to be attacked or questioned.

clue.text: Private papers distributed

indicators.note: things distributed are spread around, so these letters are scattered into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Confidential documents have been handed round to staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' reads as secret, but it is the military rank: a sapper is a private soldier in the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapper is the lowest rank of soldier in the British Royal Engineers, equivalent to a private elsewhere in the army.

clue.text: Extraordinary riches he'd clung to

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the ordinary, so these letters leave their usual order

blocks.note: the letters of the phrase, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone held on to an amazing fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Things cherished are held dear and kept close, just as things clung to are kept tight hold of.

clue.text: Honours European carrying far too much weight

blocks.note: OBEs are British honours, Officers of the Order of the British Empire
standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A European laden with medals and awards, the decorations weighing heavily on the chest.
explanation.walkthrough: An OBE is an honour awarded by the British monarch; the plural OBES gives the opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese is the medical term for a person who is seriously overweight.

clue.text: Recommend a lawyer

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, to speak in favour of
second meaning: as a noun, one who pleads cases in court

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like asking for a lawyer's name; the two halves are a verb and a noun spelt the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate is to support publicly, and an advocate is a barrister, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Give a dressing down to wicked beggars, unscrupulous opportunists

indicators.note: wicked can mean mischievous and unruly, so these letters behave badly and swap places

blocks.note: to carpet someone is to reprimand them
the word shuffled

explanation.surface: A telling-off for wicked beggars, who are dismissed as people out for what they can get.
explanation.walkthrough: To carpet is British slang for summoning someone to be scolded, from being called onto the boss's carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpetbaggers were outsiders who moved in to exploit a situation for gain, hence any unprincipled opportunist.

clue.text: Refuses to deal with villainous clerk, a rogue

blocks.note: to black goods or a firm is to boycott them in a union dispute
Uriah Heep, the scheming clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: A boss will have nothing to do with a crooked office worker who is a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Blacking is a British trade-union term for refusing to handle certain work; Uriah Heep is Dickens's oily, treacherous clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: The black sheep of a family or group is its disreputable member, a ne'er-do-well.

clue.text: Long-term prisoner describes pressure when joining book club

indicators.note: one item joining another is placed directly alongside it in sequence
to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the outer word goes around the rest

blocks.note: a lifer is serving a life sentence
P is the symbol for pressure
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: A lifer joins a reading group and talks about the strain of prison life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book club' looks like a reading circle, but 'club' alone is the definition, a cudgel.
explanation.definitionFit: A life preserver is a short weighted stick or cosh carried for self-defence, so a kind of club.

clue.text: Trade show's on also on part of cricket ground? Honestly

indicators.note: one thing being on the next places them in a line with no gap

blocks.note: a trade fair exhibits goods
and means also
the square is the central strip of a cricket field where the pitches are laid

explanation.surface: A trade exhibition is staged on a section of the cricket field, asked as a genuine question.
explanation.walkthrough: The square is the closely mown middle of a cricket ground; the question mark flags this as a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and square is an idiom meaning honestly and without cheating.

clue.text: Tree in ravine obscuring Gothic pile

indicators.note: Gothic suggests something wild and grotesque, so these letters are set in a barbarous jumble
to obscure something is to cover it up, so the outer word wraps around the inner letters

blocks.note: a chine is a deep narrow ravine, a word used on the Isle of Wight and Dorset coast
the word rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree stands in a deep valley, hiding a spooky old mansion from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gothic pile' reads as a grand house, but Gothic is the signal to rearrange the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chile pine is the monkey puzzle tree, a conifer native to Chile.

clue.text: Musical, first to captivate pianist

indicators.note: first to points at the opening letter of the following word only

blocks.note: opening letter
Dame Myra Hess, the British concert pianist

explanation.surface: A stage show that wins over the pianist from its opening number.
explanation.walkthrough: Myra Hess was famous for wartime lunchtime concerts at the National Gallery in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is the 1980s stage musical by Tim Rice with Benny and Björn of ABBA.

clue.text: Dwarf in outskirts of Sale joins up with pride

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges of a town, so only the outer letters of the word are kept
one item placed in another sits inside it
what joins is added straight on after the previous part
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: an elf is a small sprite
first and last letters
meets means joins, as roads meet

explanation.surface: A small figure on the edge of the Cheshire town of Sale links up proudly with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joins' does double duty here as the reversed word and its own linking signal; Sale is a town near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-esteem is respect for oneself, the same thing as proper pride.

clue.text: Plans to return junk mail

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: maps are plans of an area

explanation.surface: Someone arranges for unwanted circulars to be sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is unsolicited bulk email, the electronic equivalent of unwanted advertising post.

clue.text: Unfinished poem depicting two biblical characters

blocks.note: first figure: Jesus
second figure: the son of Adam slain by Cain

explanation.surface: A fragment of verse showing a pair of people from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Christabel is Coleridge's narrative poem, which he never completed.

clue.text: Working together, performing live

blocks.note: first meaning: acting jointly
second meaning: playing on stage before an audience

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a band on stage; the phrase is used both of cooperation and of live music.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert means in cooperation, and a band shown in concert is filmed during a live show.

clue.text: Release legal document showing discretion

blocks.note: to free is to let go
a will sets out how an estate is left

explanation.surface: Publishing a testament shows tact on someone's part.
explanation.definitionFit: Free will is the power to act at one's own discretion, by personal choice.

clue.text: Run out for conduit which will provide the finished article

blocks.note: to end is to run out, expire
pro means in favour of
a duct is a channel or pipe

explanation.surface: Running out of pipework is what will result in the completed product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out' looks like an anagram signal but just means finish; 'for' here is pro, as in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: An end product is the final result of a manufacturing process, the completed item.

clue.text: Man-eating monster consequently comes back

indicators.note: a word that comes back travels the opposite way, so it is read from its last letter

blocks.note: Latin ergo means therefore

explanation.surface: A cannibal beast returns as a result.
explanation.definitionFit: In fairy tales the ogre is a giant that eats people.

clue.text: He painted giant stepping across island

indicators.note: a stride across something straddles it, so the outer word spans the inner letter

blocks.note: the Titans were Greek giants
abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A painter depicted a colossus striding over an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great Venetian Renaissance painter, so the answer is the man who painted.

clue.text: Indignation shown when card game's cut short

indicators.note: a thing cut short loses its end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: piquet is a card game for two

explanation.surface: A player is annoyed when the card session is stopped early.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is a fit of wounded resentment, a kind of irritation or indignation.

clue.text: Certain to share secrets? Not without love

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following letter is taken out

blocks.note: to confide is to tell secrets
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Is someone sure about telling secrets? Not if there is no romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Certain to share secrets?' looks like a description of a confidant; only 'Certain' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Confident means sure, assured of something, the same as certain.

clue.text: Bird over northern peak

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places one item above the next in the column

blocks.note: a crow is a black bird
abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A bird flies above a mountain summit in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of a hill is its top, so crown and peak both mean summit.

clue.text: Fat spouses with a diet I prepared

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been processed and made up, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Overweight couples follow a slimming plan someone has drawn up.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose tissue is the body's fat-storing tissue, made of fat cells.

clue.text: Statesman with 'Duke'?

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
Duke Ellington, the American jazz bandleader and composer

explanation.surface: A politician who holds a ducal title, as the quotation marks and question mark tease.
explanation.walkthrough: The obvious reading is the Duke of Wellington himself, but the quoted 'Duke' is the jazzman's nickname, joined to W for with.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Wellington, victor at Waterloo, later served as a British Prime Minister, so he was a statesman.
